title: U.S. House · Oklahoma's 3rd District
area: Northwestern and western Oklahoma, the state's largest district by area, including Enid and the Panhandle

context.text: Frank Lucas and Suzie Byrd are the only candidates on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for this district.

candidates.name: Frank Lucas

summary.text: Frank Lucas is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Oklahoma's 3rd District, seeking re-election. A farmer and rancher before entering politics, he served in the Oklahoma House of Representatives before his 1994 election to Congress, and has since chaired the House Agriculture Committee and the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee. He now sits on the Agriculture and Financial Services committees and chairs the Financial Services Task Force on Monetary Policy, Treasury Market Resilience, and Economic Prosperity.

background.text: Earned a B.S. from Oklahoma State University in 1982.
Worked as a farmer and rancher before entering politics.
Served in the Oklahoma House of Representatives until his election to the U.S. House in 1994.

Won election to the U.S. House in 1994 and represented Oklahoma's 6th District until 2003; the district was renumbered as the 3rd after the 2000 Census, and he has represented the 3rd District since 2003.
Chaired the House Agriculture Committee from 2011 to 2015, after serving as its ranking member from 2009 to 2011.
Was ranking member of the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee from 2019 to 2023 and chaired it from 2023 to 2025.

In the 2025-2026 term, serves on the House Agriculture Committee (chairing its Subcommittee on Conservation, Research, and Biotechnology) and on the Financial Services Committee, and chairs the Financial Services Task Force on Monetary Policy, Treasury Market Resilience, and Economic Prosperity.

priorities.text: Advocates for fiscal responsibility, including supporting the Common Cents Act to codify an executive order on coin production.

record.text: Delivered remarks on the House floor advocating for fiscal responsibility and supporting the Common Cents Act, which would codify President Trump's order on penny production.

As chairman of the House Financial Services Task Force on Monetary Policy, Treasury Market Resilience, and Economic Prosperity, delivered the opening statement at Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's first Financial Services Committee hearing testimony.
Hosted a House Financial Services Task Force field hearing in Oklahoma City on the structure of the Federal Reserve System.

candidates.name: Suzie Byrd

summary.text: Suzie Byrd is the Democratic nominee in Oklahoma's 3rd District. According to her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, she grew up in Oklahoma, was a college athlete at Oklahoma State University, has owned or partnered in more than a dozen businesses, and worked nearly four years as a reporter for the Enid News before resigning to run for Congress. She says she is running on universal healthcare, affordable housing and a livable wage, and a fairer tax code.

background.text: Describes herself as born and raised in Oklahoma, with grandparents who farmed in southwest Oklahoma and a father who worked in the oil field.
Graduated from Hennessey High School, where she says she was an All-State athlete in basketball and track.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Oklahoma State University in 1976; says her degree is in journalism and that she played basketball one year and ran track two years, was a two-time Big 8 champion, and was the school's first female All-American.
Says she has owned or been a partner in more than 12 businesses in Oklahoma and Florida.
Says she was a reporter for the Enid News for almost four years before resigning to run for Congress, writing about education, healthcare, abuse and contamination of farmland.
Says she has two daughters and two grandchildren, lives in Enid, and built her own barn house out of an interest in affordable housing.

priorities.text: Supports universal healthcare, arguing it would save money and reduce deaths and bankruptcies linked to lack of insurance.
priorities.quote: I am for universal healthcare. Healthcare for profit has ruined our healthcare and made it unaffordable.

priorities.text: Supports affordable housing and a livable wage, including programs for first-time homebuyers.
priorities.quote: I am for affordable housing and a livable wage.

priorities.text: Says AI and data centers need regulation to safeguard resources and jobs for the future.
priorities.quote: I am very concerned about AI and Data Centers. We do not have the public policy and the information we need to plan for the future of our children and our resources.

positions.summary: Supports universal healthcare, citing cost savings and reduced deaths and bankruptcies from lack of insurance.
positions.quote: I am for universal healthcare. Healthcare for profit has ruined our healthcare and made it unaffordable.

positions.summary: Says the wealthy need to pay their fair share and opposes tax cuts that favor the rich over workers.
positions.quote: No more supply side economics and tax cuts for the rich. The wealthy need to pay their fair share and we need to make our tax code fair.

positions.summary: Supports programs for first-time homebuyers and encouraging new housing models to address affordability.
